**Finding submitted: deviation (INDEMN).**

**What the document actually has.** The only indemnity is Subparagraph 21.2 (p0241) — a fully reciprocal Party-to-Party indemnity for third-party claims arising out of ownership of APCN 2, capped at each Party's Schedule B share. Paragraph 32 (p0275–p0280) adds reimbursement proportions, a notice-to-Management-Committee condition and settlement-approval control, but only as machinery for cost sharing among Parties.

**Why it fails.** Searches for "indemnify", "patent", "infringement", "intellectual property", "supplier"/"contractor" confirm there is **no IP infringement indemnity anywhere**, and no cover for another Party's breach of law, data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct. Absence of any IP indemnity in our favour is expressly walk-away territory, and the fallback is equally unmet (no procure/modify/replace or refund remedies, and no fee anchor for a super-cap — fee-based machinery does not map onto this cost-sharing consortium structure). I therefore targeted **preferred**.

**The change (validated, ok:true, minimality gate passed).**
1. New Subparagraph 21.4 inserted at the end of Paragraph 21 (after p0245): each other Party defends and indemnifies us and our affiliates against third-party claims for IP infringement in anything it provides, its breach of applicable law, data breach it causes, and its gross negligence or wilful misconduct — with notice, control of defence, and reasonable cooperation. No survival tail, expense or damages boilerplate added.
2. A short proviso appended verbatim-preserving inside 21.2, limiting **our** indemnity to content we provide and our own breach of law. Every existing word of 21.2, including the Schedule B share cap, is retained; Paragraph 32's sharing and settlement mechanics are untouched, so no cross-reference is left dangling.
